The "Apollo 13" film, according to AR module pilot Ken Mattingly (who was replaced by Jack Swigert just before the mission), misrepresented Swigert as being unprepared for the flight. In reality, Swigert was very familiar with the module, having worked on its development. The dialogue in the film was taken nearly verbatim from transcripts and recordings, with the exception of the line "Houston, we have a problem." The actual words spoken by Swigert were "Okay, Houston, we've had a problem here."

Another inaccuracy in the film is the dialogue after the re-entry blackout. In the movie, Tom Hanks (as Jim Lovell) says "Hello Houston... this is Odyssey... it's good to see you again." However, in reality, the Command Module's transmission was acquired by a Sikorsky SH-3D Sea King recovery helicopter, which then relayed communications to Mission Control. CAPCOM astronaut Joe Kerwin (not Mattingly, who serves as CAPCOM in this scene in the film) made a call to the spacecraft "Odyssey, Houston standing by. Over." Swigert, not Lovell, replied "Okay, Joe," and this was well before the parachutes deployed.

The tagline "Failure is not an option" was not actually said during the Apollo 13 mission, but it has since become a popular catchphrase.

According to audio of the air-to-ground communications, the actual words uttered by Swigert were "Okay, Houston, we've had a problem here". Ground control responded by saying, "This is Houston. Say again, please." Jim Lovell then repeated, "Houston, we've had a problem." One other incorrect dialogue is after the re-entry blackout.
